caption: In re Horizon Healthcare Services Inc. Data Breach Litigation
citation_line: In re Horizon Healthcare Services Inc. Data Breach Litigation, No. 2:13-cv-07418, ECF No. 47 (D.N.J. Mar. 31, 2015), vacated, 846 F.3d 625 (3d Cir. 2017)
headnote_district_ruling: Judge Cecchi dismissed a putative class action arising from the theft of laptops containing personal and health information, concluding that the plaintiffs had not alleged a cognizable injury because they did not show actual misuse of the data.
qualification_rationale: The appeal became an important post-Spokeo standing decision. It held that an alleged violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act can constitute a concrete injury even without demonstrated misuse of the stolen information, and it remains influential in data-breach standing disputes.
appellate_posture_note: The Third Circuit vacated and remanded in a precedential opinion, holding that Congress had created a remedy for unauthorized transfers of personal information and that the alleged disclosure itself supplied Article III injury.
subject_label: Data Privacy and Article III Standing
decision_selection_note: The opinion behind ECF 48/50. You appeal from the order; the reasoning the Third Circuit vacated at 846 F.3d 625 is here. ECF 157 is the 2021 re-dismissal after remand.
